messages:
maria: FYI ran the FP8-KV vs INT8-KV bakeoff on the chat LLM we onboarded last week. baseline = float16 everywhere. results below, short thread with configs and a couple hypotheses.

raj: nice — can you drop the perf table? :eyes:

maria: paste: 
```
model: chat-xxl-v1
workload: 512-token chat, batch=1, concurrent=50
configs:
  - baseline: fp16-all
  - int8-kv: int8 for KV tensors, fp16 elsewhere
  - fp8-kv: fp8 (E4M3) for KV, fp16 elsewhere
metrics (p50/p95 tokens/ms and mem footprint):
  baseline: p50=12ms p95=34ms mem=28.4GB
  int8-kv: p50=12.5ms p95=36ms mem=22.3GB (-21%)
  fp8-kv: p50=12.9ms p95=46ms mem=20.5GB (-28%)
quality (LM eval on eval-suite-A): ppl/delta from baseline
  baseline: ppl=13.2
  int8-kv: ppl=13.5 (+2.3%)
  fp8-kv: ppl=14.1 (+6.8%)
cold-start tail (first-token p95): baseline=75ms, int8-kv=92ms, fp8-kv=125ms
```

oliver: whoa fp8 KV memory win is great but cold-start p95 hit is concerning. any traces?

maria: traced kernels. FP8 path introduces an extra dequant/repack on first KV fill; subsequent tokens amortize it (steady-state p95 is close to baseline). cold-start cost = ~28ms extra for dequant + ~22ms for extra cuda memcpy because we changed layout to compact.

tess: can we mitigate with async prefetch/warmup? warmup on router side?

maria: tried two mitigations: (A) local synchronous KV warmup on first request (send 1 extra decode step to populate cache) -> reduces cold p95 for fp8-kv from 125ms -> 98ms but adds ~1x extra compute on first query. (B) background async prefetch from prefix hash when request arrives -> reduces to 84ms with almost no extra compute but needs router support.

raj: do we have rollout profile that avoids hitting this for PLG traffic? maybe enable fp8-kv only for dedicated pools where warmup can be managed.

maria: agreed. for hosted we should prefer int8-kv as default: smaller mem win than fp8 but much friendlier tail. propose rollout matrix: 
- Hosted: int8-kv default, fp8-kv opt-in for dedicated customers with warmup toggles
- Dedicated: allow fp8-kv when customer enables background warmup or low-cold constraints
- Private: recommend fp8-kv with HWM checks and eviction tuning

oliver: curious about accuracy delta per task. ppl up ~6.8% for fp8-kv — how does that map to question-answer F1?

maria: quick eval on SQuAD-lite: baseline F1=88.3, int8-kv=87.6 (-0.8 abs), fp8-kv=86.1 (-2.2 abs). so degradation is nontrivial for extraction tasks. open-domain chat subjective eval shows more hallucination in fp8-kv.

benchbot: x-bench: full run (1000 samples) completed. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/bench/1911112222-fp8kv-vs-int8 (internal) :bar_chart:

tess: +1 on dashboard link, can we add an automated guard in the model catalog? flag models where fp8-kv causes >2% QA drop or >10ms cold p95 delta.

maria: yes i added rules locally and a check in the onboarding eval harness. PR coming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/482 (WIP). includes auto-eval against SQuAD-lite + chat-hedged prompts.

raj: ops note: fp8-kv changes memory layout; rolling kernels will need kube node image bump. we'll need a migration plan for dedicated clusters. ping @tess for rollout comms.

tess: will coordinate. Also recommending adding a small warmup token on client SDK for first request (configurable) to reduce user-facing tails.

oliver: last q — any sign of catastrophic numerical instability? e.g., NaNs or extreme logits?

maria: no NaNs in 1000-sample run. we do see slight logit scaling drift; fixed via per-layer scale calibration (we used per-channel 🤏). that cut ppl delta by ~1.5% for fp8-kv. details in PR notes.

raj: next steps checklist: 
- maria: finalize PR with calibration and warmup recipes
- benchbot: run extended 10k sample perf+quality sweep under mixed concurrency
- ops (raj/tess): draft rollout docs and cluster image changes
- product: decide default catalog policy (int8-kv vs fp8-kv opt-in)

maria: adding a note — hybrid-profile where KV=FP8 but projection heads remain INT8 (or fp16) looked promising in small tests: mem ~ -26% and ppl +4% (vs fp8-kv +6.8%). might be a good compromise.

oliver: thanks — this is actionable. :thumbsup:

tess: can someone paste the short command we used to run the bench? for runbook.

maria: command: `./bench/run.sh --model chat-xxl-v1 --profile fp8-kv --concurrency 50 --seq 512 --samples 1000 --warmup off`

raj: and the warmup-config we tested: 
```
warmup:
  strategy: async-prefetch
  prefetch_size: 8
  timeout_ms: 40
```

benchbot: note: scheduled extended-run at 1911116000 (UTC) to gather mixed-burst metrics.

maria: will follow up with PR link, extended-run results, and proposed catalog guard. thanks all. :party_parrot:

oliver: +1, excited to see the extended numbers.
